lines.en: Zoe, I was going to call you last night, but my phone died. You did not worry, did you?
lines.pt: Zoe, eu ia ligar para você ontem à noite, mas meu celular descarregou. Você não se preocupou, preocupou?

lines.en: A little. Your mother told me you would be here by six, and it is already half past, isn’t it?
lines.pt: Um pouco. Sua mãe me disse que você estaria aqui às seis, e já são seis e meia, não são?

lines.en: Yes, sorry. We were about to leave the hotel when the taxi driver called to say he would be late.
lines.pt: Sim, desculpe. Estávamos prestes a sair do hotel quando o motorista de táxi ligou para dizer que se atrasaria.

lines.en: Typical. Nobody tells us the truth about taxis, do they? Anyway, check the timetable, shall we? Platform four, I think.
lines.pt: Típico. Ninguém nos conta a verdade sobre táxis, conta? Enfim, vamos ver a tabela de horários, certo? Plataforma quatro, acho.

lines.en: Right. I was going to book seats online, but the website crashed, so we have to buy tickets here, don’t we?
lines.pt: Certo. Eu ia reservar lugares pela internet, mas o site caiu, então precisamos comprar passagens aqui, não é?

lines.en: We do. The ticket office said it would open a second window by ten, but nobody is here yet.
lines.pt: Precisamos. A bilheteria disse que abriria um segundo guichê às dez, mas ainda não tem ninguém.

lines.en: Nobody ever is, are they? I was about to give up and take the bus when you wrote to me.
lines.pt: Nunca tem ninguém, tem? Eu estava prestes a desistir e pegar o ônibus quando você me escreveu.

lines.en: I am glad you did not. When I booked the hostel, they promised that the room would be ready by noon.
lines.pt: Que bom que não desistiu. Quando reservei o hostel, prometeram que o quarto estaria pronto ao meio-dia.

lines.en: Let’s not waste time, shall we? Carry this bag, will you? The train is about to leave, I can hear the whistle.
lines.pt: Vamos não perder tempo, certo? Carregue esta bolsa, pode ser? O trem está prestes a sair, ouço o apito.

lines.en: Run, then! We were about to miss it, and you would have been angry with me for the rest of the week.
lines.pt: Corra, então! Estávamos prestes a perdê-lo, e você ficaria brava comigo pelo resto da semana.

lines.en: I would never have been angry, We made it, didn’t we? Next time, I will call you first.
lines.pt: Eu nunca ficaria brava, Conseguimos, não foi? Da próxima vez, ligo para você primeiro.

facts.label: Plans that changed
facts.sub: was going to · would · about to · tag questions

facts.label: I was going to call
facts.sub: Use was/were going to + verbo para um plano que não se realizou: I was going to call you, but my phone died. Em geral aparece com but.

facts.label: she said she would
facts.sub: No relato do passado, will vira would: Your mother told me you would be here by six. Também usamos would para o que esperávamos que acontecesse.

compare.ask: I was going to call you, but my phone died.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “eu ia ligar”, “ela disse que viria” e “está prestes a sair”.
compare.tip: Diga: “I was going to call you, but my phone died.”
compare.us: Em inglês: I was going to call; she said she would come; it is about to leave. Para checar, use tags: did they? shall we? will you?

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: I was going to call you means I did not call you.
She said she will come is the usual way to report in the past.
The train is about to leave is about now.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: I was going to call you means I did not call you. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
She said she will come is the usual way to report in the past. → Falso (We say she would come.)
The train is about to leave is about now. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: Plans that changed · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a busy Saturday morning in Dallas. Zoe waits near the platform with a coffee. Elena comes running through the big hall. Her phone has no battery. A voice announces the next train. The friends have a lot to explain.

“Zoe, I was going to call you last night, but my phone died. You did not worry, did you?” says Elena. “A little. Your mother told me you would be here by six, and it is already half past, isn’t it?” says Zoe. “Yes, sorry. We were about to leave the hotel when the taxi driver called to say he would be late.” says Elena.
